summary: Jowita Kramer works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She completed an MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, and habilitated at Munich. She was appointed professor at the University of Leipzig in 2021.

Joy Brennan specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard Rosengarten, and Constance Furey, and studied with traditional teacher Diane Martin.

Joyce Burkhalter Flueckiger is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Goshen College and the University of Wisconsin-Madison. From around 1986, she served at Emory University, where she is Professor Emerita.

Joydeb Dinda works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute by 2022, when he became Assistant Professor at Laxmi Devi Shroff Adarsh Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya.

Jozef Deleu was an Indologist who studied at Ghent University under Adriaan Scharpé and at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring and Ludwig Alsdorf. He taught at several institutions before serving as docent in Indology at Ghent University (1964–1990).

João Carlos Barbosa Gonçalves specializes in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He earned his PhD in linguistics at the University of São Paulo (2005–2009) and served as professor at the State University of Campinas (2003–2005) and the University of São Paulo (2014–2015).

Juan Gelabert y Gordiola was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his PhD at Complutense University of Madrid by 1868 and studied under Francisco García Ayuso. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Complutense University of Madrid from 1883 to 1894.
Juan Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Cardiff University under the supervision of Max Deeg (attested 2012).

Judit Törzsök is an Indologist who earned her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. She was Associate Professor at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III and became directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2018.

Judith Simmer-Brown is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who completed a PhD at Walden University. Beginning in 1977, she held a long-term post at Naropa University, where she became Distinguished Professor Emerita.

Judith Snodgrass is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her BA and PhD from the University of Sydney and served as Associate Professor at Western Sydney University from 1991 to 2016.

Juhn Y. Ahn specializes in Buddhist studies and earned a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 2007. He joined the University of Michigan, where he was attested as Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies in 2019.
Juhyung Rhi works in Buddhist studies, art history, and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. In 1992, he became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University.
Juichiro Tanabe is a scholar in philosophy who was a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford from 2000 to 2001 and studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He served as professor of Greek and Latin philosophy at the Collège de France (1838–1852) and was a member of the Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques (1838–1872).

Jules Bloch was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Meillet, Lévi, and Foucher, earning a doctorate from Paris. He held chairs at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, INALCO, and the Collège de France (1936–1951).

Jules Brooks Levinson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held a post as Assistant Professor in religion at Hamline University, attested in 1996.

Jules Luquiens was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Yale University under William Dwight Whitney. He taught French at MIT (1875–1892) and served as Professor of Modern Languages at Yale University from 1892 to 1899.

Jules Marouzeau was a linguist who studied at the Sorbonne under Antoine Meillet. He served as directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from 1920 and as Professor of Latin at the Sorbonne from 1925 to 1948.

Jules Michelet was a French historian who studied at Lycée Charlemagne. He held teaching posts at the École Normale Supérieure, headed a section at the Archives nationales (1830–1851), and was Professor of History at the Collège de France (1838–1852).
